source.title: How Do Transformers Learn Variable Binding in Symbolic Programs?
source.authors: Yi-Wei Wu; Atticus Geiger; Raphael Milliere

record.file_problem: The paper text is substantially complete. Some figure labels and plotted values are garbled in the extracted text; figure-only results are marked accordingly.
record.tranche_reason: The study tracks staged test-accuracy changes on a synthetic symbolic program task and uses a different method—causal patching across checkpoints—to examine the development of a generalizing mechanism. It does not reproduce modular-arithmetic grokking.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a training trajectory and mechanistic results on its own synthetic variable-dereferencing task. It does not test smaller training sets or compare delay across training-set sizes. Detailed plotted patching values that cannot be read from the extracted figures are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: This is a variable-binding interpretability study, not a grokking experiment. It trains on 450,000 programs and reports test accuracy only. The phase 2 jump (steps 800–1200) comes within the first epoch, about 7,000 steps at batch 64, so it cannot follow memorization. No training-accuracy curve, train/test gap or dataset-size sweep is reported. The staged transitions are ordinary phase-wise learning on a large dataset, not generalization delayed beyond overfitting. The line-1 heuristic is a generalizing shortcut that raises test accuracy, not a memorizing component. The authors do say their result 'adds nuance to the traditional narrative about grokking'. That is a discussion point drawn from a non-grokking setting, so I record it under fits_no_version rather than as a test of V1 or V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that the Transformer learns variable binding through three phases (random numbers, early-line heuristics, systematic dereferencing), using the residual stream as addressable memory routed by specific attention heads. They stress that the final solution builds on the early heuristics rather than replacing them, which they say nuances the grokking narrative.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a GPT-2-like model from scratch on 450,000 synthetic variable-assignment programs and analyzes causal information routing; it does not use the original modular-arithmetic grokking setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported mechanism and patching success vary with referential depth and answer-line position: deeper-hop signals emerge later and are weaker, while the line-1 heuristic persists and the line-2 heuristic is temporary.

fits_no_version.finding: On a large synthetic dataset, test accuracy rises in three sharp phases (12% → 56% → >99.9%), reproducible across six seeds. A general dereferencing circuit, tracked by checkpoint patching, emerges during phase 3. The line-1 heuristic stays active throughout (>80% patching success), while the line-2 heuristic is used only early.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Staged learning without memorization: sharp transitions between heuristic and systematic solutions occur without a train/test gap, and the later general mechanism augments rather than replaces earlier shortcut heuristics.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper gives variablescope.org as an interactive results platform
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 267, 2025
record.problems: The main mechanistic analysis centers on one 37.8M-parameter model; multiple random seeds are reported only for behavioral learning curves. The study does not report paired training-accuracy dynamics needed to establish training saturation before test improvement, nor a training-set-size sweep. Several patching results are available only in plots whose exact values are not recoverable from the extracted text.
record.rows_left_out: Fine-grained head-by-head patching plots in Figure 3 and Appendix K, and additional plot-only breakdowns in Figure 4, are not separately listed because their individual values are not legible in the extracted text; the main text descriptions and representative developmental conditions are retained.

untested.parts: No small dataset, no training-accuracy saturation before the test jump, no dataset-size sweep.
No memorization phase. The circuit tracked is not tied to delayed generalization, and there are no Fourier or memorization-removal measures.

missing.what: A model trained with 10% of variable/number combinations held out matches full-data test accuracy throughout training. This is evidence against a memorization phase.
missing.versions: none (context for why V1 is not tested)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V1/V2 labels are not supported. The setting lacks the defining feature of grokking, generalization long after training accuracy saturates. Training accuracy is never reported, and the first jump happens within one epoch of a 450k-example dataset. The authors' grokking remark concerns heuristics being discarded, but those heuristics are generalizing shortcuts, not memorization, so it does not engage V2. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports test accuracy over training on an algorithmic task, but does not report that training accuracy reached perfection before test improvement, does not use a small training set (it reports 450,000 training programs), and does not vary training-set size to test its effect on delay.

The study tracks gradual emergence of a causal variable-tracing mechanism, but does not show that memorizing components are removed; it reports that early heuristics persist. It does not use Fourier progress measures.
No non-algorithmic datasets or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
No comparison of weight decay or low-norm bias, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Multiple seeds are compared for behavioral learning curves, but the study does not identify or compare the algorithms learned across runs.
No test of adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifacts.

rows.note: The authors describe this as approximately chance-level performance. The text does not state a numerical chance baseline.

rows.note: The paper attributes this phase to early-line heuristics.

rows.subject: 37.8M-parameter Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Train on synthetic variable-dereferencing programs and evaluate test accuracy across training phases.
rows.value: jumps to 99%; eventually exceeds 99.9% on the test set
rows.note: This is a delayed rise in test accuracy on the task, but the paper does not establish its timing relative to perfect training accuracy.
rows.check: The 56% to 99% transition has no paired training accuracy and comes from a 450k-example dataset. It shows staged learning, not V1's delay beyond overfitting.

rows.subject: 37.8M-parameter Transformer (six training runs, aggregate as described by the authors)

rows.note: Aggregate statement about the six runs; no exact curve values are legible in the extracted figure.
rows.check: Seed reproducibility of test-accuracy phases. It says nothing about grokking delay or about the learned algorithm (V6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The reported synthetic variable-dereferencing task and training runs
reader_labels.reason: Test accuracy rises in stages from approximately 12% to above 99.9%, but the study uses 450,000 training programs and does not show training accuracy saturating first or test delay increasing as the dataset shrinks (r1–r4).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The causal patching signals emerge across training at task-relevant RHS and query positions, with the text describing delayed emergence at greater depths (r5–r8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The study reports that the line-1 heuristic remains active throughout training while the general mechanism is added for cases requiring it; the line-2 heuristic is only used in the initial phase. This qualifies an account in which memorizing components are later removed (r9–r10).
